title: Several things look wrong in a race recording (agateau/pixelwheels #362, temporal_interaction)
verdict_reason: One dimension fails: Tests – Implementation Overfit (dim 11, [Fail - Overfit Tests]). RocketTest and MissileZOrderTest build the shooter as mock(Racer.class) and stub only getVehicle()/getPosition(). So a correct fix that tints the carried missile with its vehicle's colour, exactly as the repo's own Mine.draw tints a carried mine (Mine.java:181), crashes 3 of the 7 f2p with a NullPointerException. Verified locally: golden + that one tint block = reward 0.0 (f2p 4/7); the same code with the two mocks stubbed = 1.0 (7/7). Trial jmtBZi2 wrote this tint and lost exactly those 3 f2p to the same NPE. Difficulty, the Attempt3 failure, now passes: 0/3 no-image and exactly 1/4 with-image (afXQArC). Symptom Specificity scores 3 [Non-Fail - Image-carried Symptom], which is not a fail. The new wording states the z-order and shadow defects in text and removes the Attempt3 misreading (every with-image run now names the rocket over the footbridge as a bug). The rocket's orientation, its flame and the camera stay image-carried. The other 17 dimensions score 5. Local oracle 1.0, nop 0.0, re-run identical.

dimensions.evidence: Attempt4/Tasks/agateau__pixelwheels_362_mm has all 11 fixed files, none empty: task.toml 5988 B, instruction.md 948 B, evidence_bundle.json 1859 B, environment/Dockerfile 3063 B, environment/assets/ASSET_MANIFEST.json 605 B, solution/fix.patch 8587 B, solution/solve.sh 349 B, tests/config.json 1450 B, tests/test.patch 59246 B, tests/test.sh 11141 B, tests/verifier.py 8482 B. All three JSON files parse (json.load) and tests/verifier.py passes py_compile. The asset recording.mp4 (4717379 B) decodes in the task image: ffprobe gives 1920x1080, 30/1 fps, 345 frames read, duration 11.5 s. The extras environment/bugs/bug_01..05.patch are injected-bug patches that the Dockerfile applies and deletes in the same RUN, which is allowed. README.md is also extra. Compared with Attempt3, only instruction.md changed (sha256 a5a7b246 vs 83baf7c0); the other 17 files are byte-identical, and the stray tests/__pycache__/verifier.cpython-313.pyc from Attempt3 is gone.

dimensions.name: Instruction – Requires Visual Evidence
dimensions.evidence: Read without the video, instruction.md gives three kinds of problem: carried things 'drawn or hidden wrongly compared with that vehicle', shadows that 'don't fall or turn like the others', and a race view that 'doesn't follow the action the way it should'. It adds one concrete symptom, new in Attempt4: 'it can show through something that covers the vehicle'. It names no object, timestamp, file, repo or mechanism. The no-image trials show the text is not enough for a complete fix. In every no-image run /app/.harbor_assets was empty (step 3: 'total 8', only . and ..), and each scored f2p 4/7. All three fixed the z-order, both shadows and the camera from the text plus a code audit. All three missed carriedRocketPointsWhereTheCarPoints, firedRocketFliesWhereTheCarPoints and rocketExhaustComesOutOfItsTail, so the rocket orientation and flame defects (bugs 01-03) still need the video. The path resolves: the Dockerfile has `COPY assets/recording.mp4 /app/.harbor_assets/` and the in-image sha256 is 976eac49...ce179. Leak check: instruction.md names no repo, URL, file list or mechanism. The mechanism appears only in task.toml, which is blind (task_manifest.json blind list: tests/, solution/, task.toml).
dimensions.wrong: Nothing found. Non-graded: the new parenthetical makes the z-order defect solvable from the text alone. 3/3 no-image runs fixed missileIsDrawnBeforeForegroundLayer, against 0/3 in Attempt3, so only 3 of the 7 f2p (2 of the 6 defects) now depend on the video. V27 is fine with that. task.toml difficulty_explanation is now stale: it still quotes the Attempt3 wording ('things that go along with a vehicle', 'shadows that do not match what casts them') and still says 'Without the video the instruction gives no symptom to search for'.
dimensions.fix: None required. Optional: update difficulty_explanation to the Attempt4 wording, and say that the z-order symptom is now in the text. Editing task.toml changes the checksum, so batch it with the test.patch fix from dim 11.

dimensions.name: Instruction – Symptom Specificity
dimensions.evidence:
WHAT CHANGED vs Attempt3 (instruction.md is the only changed file): 'Some of the things that go along with a vehicle are drawn or hidden wrongly compared with that vehicle' became 'Some of what a vehicle carries is drawn or hidden wrongly compared with that vehicle (it can show through something that covers the vehicle)'. 'some shadows don't match what casts them' became 'some shadows don't fall or turn like the others in the clip'. 'keep looking the way it does now' became '... the way they do now'.
TABLE (element | defect: text or image? | expected: text or image? | comparison pointed to | clue left to image | described correctly?)
1. 'what a vehicle carries' (the rocket on the car, its flight and its flame) | z-order: TEXT, 'it can show through something that covers the vehicle'. Orientation (crosswise on the car 0-1.2 s; fired south into the fence at 9.9 s) and flame (out of the rocket's side at 9.9 s): kind only, 'drawn ... wrongly compared with that vehicle'; the exact defect is in the IMAGE | z-order: implied in text (hidden along with the vehicle). Orientation and flame: IMAGE, via 'the same kind of thing is drawn correctly elsewhere in the same clip' (the car itself is hidden by the bridge; the car's boost flame comes from its back at 6.6-7.0 s) | in-clip comparison | which object (rocket), what covers it (footbridge), when, how far off | yes, checked on sheet_2 (countdown), sheet_4b (footbridge) and sheet_5 (launch). Minor: once fired, the rocket is no longer carried, so 'what a vehicle carries ... compared with that vehicle' covers the fired-direction and flame defects only loosely. It is not false.
2. 'some shadows' | TEXT: 'don't fall or turn like the others' | TEXT + IMAGE: like the others in the clip | in-clip comparison | which shadows (car shadow up-left in the countdown; rocket and crate shadows that don't rotate) | yes. This fixes the Attempt3 looseness, where 'don't match what casts them' did not describe the car shadow, which has the right shape but falls on the wrong side.
3. 'the race view' | kind only: 'doesn't follow the action the way it should' | IMAGE (north/south stretches vs east/west straights; at 8 s the car is at the left edge heading west) | in-clip comparison | which stretches, which direction | yes.
THE THREE CHECKS: (1) an element is named for all three areas, with no fix hint. (2) every general phrase comes with its context right away (compared with that vehicle / like the others / follow the action), plus the in-clip pointer. (3) the clues (which instance, when, how big) stay in the clip. The defect is stated in text for the z-order and both shadows. For the rocket's orientation, its flame and the camera, the exact defect is left to in-clip comparisons. That is the [Non-Fail - Image-carried Symptom] pattern, not a 5.
TRAJECTORIES (all 4 with-image runs read in full): every run named the rocket drawn over the footbridge as a bug: cM2qDRx step 17 ('A carried missile showed through the bridge'), YXypWaB steps 21 and 26, jmtBZi2 steps 7 and 33, afXQArC steps 14 and 19. The Attempt3 misreading (wewmugH: 'already behave as the code intends') does not recur. All 4 found both shadow defects and the camera defect. The crosswise rocket was noticed by jmtBZi2 (step 20 'attached sideways (crosswise to the car)', step 25 'Confirmed in close-up') and afXQArC (step 14 'mounted sideways'). cM2qDRx and YXypWaB never mention it: they looked only at 2 fps 3x4 tile sheets plus a crop around the bridge. Only afXQArC fixed the side flame, and nobody else mentions it. A grep of all 4 runs for 'intended', 'by design', 'looks fine/right/correct', 'not a bug' and 'left ... alone' finds no defect described as intended. The misses are perception misses (silence), not misreadings.
dimensions.wrong: Not a fail. Flag for feedback: [Non-Fail - Image-carried Symptom]. The text states the z-order and shadow defects, but the rocket's orientation, its flight direction, its flame and the camera's look-ahead appear only as a kind of problem; the exact defect is left to in-clip comparisons. RISK, not scored: 2 of the 4 with-image runs (cM2qDRx, YXypWaB) never mention the crosswise rocket, although it fills the 0-1.2 s countdown close-up. A strict reviewer could read that silence as 'agents could not tell the bug from intended behavior'. The rubric needs the trials to show that, and no run does: none calls any defect intended. This is a clear improvement on Attempt3, where wewmugH explicitly ruled the footbridge defect intended.
dimensions.fix: None required. If you edit instruction.md anyway (the dim 11 fix already forces a re-run of every trial), a line that would reach 5 without naming any object, cause or timestamp is: 'Some of what a vehicle carries is drawn wrongly compared with that vehicle: it can show through something that covers the vehicle, or not face the way the vehicle faces; and the race view doesn't keep the road ahead in view whichever way the car drives.' Warning: clearer text raises the with-image pass rate (now exactly 1/4) and the no-image fix rate. Changing instruction.md changes the task checksum, so all 7 trials must be re-run.

dimensions.name: Instruction – Task Type
dimensions.evidence: task_type = temporal_interaction: 'Fix a defect that only appears across a sequence of interactions / state transitions'. The defects the text describes show up across transitions in the clip. The rocket shows over the footbridge only while the car passes under it (9.25-9.33 s). The fired rocket's path and flame appear only after launch (9.9-10.2 s). The look-ahead error depends on the heading as the lap goes on (east/west vs north/south stretches). The Attempt4 wording (carried things showing through a cover, shadows that don't fall or turn like the others, a view that doesn't follow the action) describes drawing and view problems in a recorded race, which fits the type.
dimensions.wrong: Nothing found. Two of the six defects (the crosswise rocket and the car shadow) are visible in a single frame. That is fine, since the task as a whole needs the sequence.

dimensions.name: Image – Evidence Quality
dimensions.evidence: The asset is byte-identical to Attempt3 (sha256 976eac49...ce179, 4717379 B), so the frame analysis carries over. It was re-checked here on the contact sheets in evidence/. NAMING TABLE (file | role | what the frames show | what name/role/text claim | true? | agents confused?): recording.mp4 | bug_video | base behavior with bugs 01-05 injected. 0-1.2 s countdown: rocket crosswise on a north-facing car, car shadow up-left (sheet_2). 9.18-9.40 s: car hidden under the footbridge while the rocket and a flat rocket shadow are drawn over it (sheet_4b). 9.75-10.2 s: rocket fired, heading south into the fence while the car heads west, flame on its side, explodes at the fence at 10.05 s (sheet_5). 6.6-7.0 s: the car's own boost flame comes out of its back (sheet_3). 8 s: car at the left edge heading west (sheet_1) | neutral name; role 'bug_video'; the ASSET_MANIFEST and evidence_bundle descriptions (countdown, lap, footbridge, launch, explosion at the fence) | true | no: no run treated the video as a reference. All 4 with-image runs read the footbridge frames as the bug, and jmtBZi2 and afXQArC read the crosswise rocket correctly. F2P vs ASSET (steps 1-4): missileIsDrawnBeforeForegroundLayer ↔ rocket over the bridge (sheet_4b); fixing only that, by drawing the carried rocket at the car's level as cM2qDRx, YXypWaB and afXQArC did, passes the f2p. carriedRocketPointsWhereTheCarPoints ↔ crosswise rocket (sheet_2). firedRocketFliesWhereTheCarPoints ↔ rocket flying south into the fence (sheet_5). rocketExhaustComesOutOfItsTail ↔ side flame (sheet_5). rocketShadowHasTheRocketsOrientation ↔ flat rocket shadow (sheet_4b); the crate shadows also fail to rotate, and all 4 with-image agents used them. vehicleShadowFallsLikeEveryOtherShadow ↔ car shadow up-left (sheet_2). viewLooksAheadOfTheCarWhicheverWayItHeads ↔ road behind the car on the east/west straights (sheet_1, 8 s). Each f2p scenario (several headings, carried and fired, a foreground tile above) contains the state the clip shows. STEP 7 (injected defects, bugs 01-05): a fix that skips any of them leaves a defect visible in the clip, so it is incomplete, not a valid alternative. The upstream #362 symptom (rocket over the footbridge) is what the clip shows. The dim 11 problem comes from the test mocks, not from a gap between evidence and f2p, so it does not touch this dimension.

dimensions.name: Tests – Implementation Overfit
dimensions.evidence:
The assertions themselves are behavioral and tolerant: recorded draw order and quad geometry from a DrawRecorder batch, Box2D positions and the camera offset, with angle tolerances (< 5° for the rocket nose and travel, < 2° for the shadow) and positional ones. None compares a string, enum or format, so there is no output-form issue. The problem is the harness. RocketTest (test.patch line 152) and MissileZOrderTest (line 720) create the shooter as `Racer racer = mock(Racer.class)` and stub only getVehicle()/getPosition(), so every other Racer getter returns null. In the real game Racer.getVehicleRenderer() is never null: Racer.java:127 has `mVehicleRenderer = new VehicleRenderer(assets, mVehicle)`. The repo's own carried item calls it while drawing: Mine.java:181 has `batch.setColor(mOwner.getVehicleRenderer().getBatchColor())` for an attached mine, followed by `batch.setColor(Color.WHITE)`. GunBonus:102/165 and TurboBonus:75/108 call it too.
EQUIVALENCE TABLE (alternative | correct & in repo context? | test accepts? | evidence):
(A) golden ZLevel split (FLYING_LOW / FG_LAYERS / FLYING_HIGH) | yes | yes | local oracle and re-run 7/7, 2/2.
(B) carried missile drawn at its vehicle's ZLevel, fired missile on top | yes, plausible | yes | cM2qDRx, YXypWaB and afXQArC pass missileIsDrawnBeforeForegroundLayer.
(C) golden + tint the carried missile with its vehicle's batch colour, as Mine.draw does: `if (mStatus == Status.WAITING) batch.setColor(mShooter.getVehicleRenderer().getBatchColor());` before drawShadow/drawMissile, then `batch.setColor(Color.WHITE)` | yes. It fixes the whole issue (golden untouched). It respects the repo's contracts (a public getter that is never null in game; p2p 2/2). It is plausible (it copies Mine.draw line for line). It matches the evidence: getBatchColor() returns WHITE unless the car is sinking (VehicleRenderer.java:68-77), so every recorded frame is unchanged. It is arguably more complete: without it, a carried missile still shows through the water covering a sinking car, which is the instruction's own 'it can show through something that covers the vehicle' | NO | local run alt_tint: reward 0.0, f2p 4/7. missileIsDrawnBeforeForegroundLayer, carriedRocketPointsWhereTheCarPoints and rocketShadowHasTheRocketsOrientation all fail with 'NullPointerException: Cannot invoke VehicleRenderer.getBatchColor() because the return value of Racer.getVehicleRenderer() is null' at Missile.draw. The same code with the two mocks stubbed (alt_tint_stubbed): 1.0, 7/7, 2/2. TRIAL EVIDENCE: jmtBZi2 wrote this tint ('dims with the car when it falls into water', step 33) and lost exactly those 3 f2p to the same NPE (its junit.xml). A local replay of its submission.patch reproduces 0.0 with f2p 3/7.
(D) rocket angle: golden degRad / vehicle.getBody().getAngle() / referenceAngle = 0 | yes | yes | afXQArC (degreesToRadians) passed; jmtBZi2 (getBody().getAngle()) passed firedRocketFliesWhereTheCarPoints, and also carriedRocketPointsWhereTheCarPoints once the mocks are stubbed (replay 6/7).
(E) exhaust by cos/sin (golden) or Vector2(refH, 0).rotateRad | yes, same vector | yes | afXQArC.
(F) shadow angle radDeg in BodyRegionDrawer, with or without the extra scale fix | yes | yes | all 4 with-image runs.
(G) car shadow sign flip | yes | yes | all 4 with-image runs.
(H) look-ahead as (advance, 0).rotate(a) or (0, advance).rotate(a - 90), with or without moving the camera speed clamp | yes, same vector | yes | all 4 with-image runs passed viewLooksAheadOfTheCarWhicheverWayItHeads.
RESULT: (C) is a valid, plausible and correct alternative that 3 of the 7 f2p reject for a reason unrelated to the graded behavior.
dimensions.wrong: 3 of the 7 f2p (missileIsDrawnBeforeForegroundLayer, carriedRocketPointsWhereTheCarPoints, rocketShadowHasTheRocketsOrientation) reject a correct fix written another way. The cause is the harness: the mocked Racer returns null for getVehicleRenderer(), a public getter that the real game always fills and that the repo's own carried mine uses in its draw(). The fix's behavior is not the problem. A fix that tints the carried missile like the carried mine scores 0.0. It did not change this batch's outcome: replaying jmtBZi2's submission under the stubbed tests gives 6/7, still 0.0, because it really missed the exhaust. The 1/4 with-image result stands, but the tests are coupled to an implementation detail (that Missile.draw never asks the shooter for its renderer), and a real trial hit it.
dimensions.fix: Stub the renderer on both mocked racers. In RocketTest.java and MissileZOrderTest.java, right after `when(racer.getVehicle()).thenReturn(vehicle);` (test.patch lines 153 and 721), add `VehicleRenderer renderer = mock(VehicleRenderer.class); when(renderer.getBatchColor()).thenReturn(Color.WHITE); when(racer.getVehicleRenderer()).thenReturn(renderer);` plus the imports. Then regenerate test.patch from the edited sources, since added lines change the hunk headers. Verified locally with this stub (written inline on the same line): golden 1.0 (7/7, 2/2), nop 0.0 (0/7, 2/2, same assertion messages), golden + tint 1.0, jmtBZi2 replay 6/7. Also check other getters a carried-item fix may reasonably call (e.g. gameWorld.getTrack(), which Mine.draw uses). Changing test.patch changes the task checksum, so re-run Oracle, Nop and all 7 trials.

dimensions.name: Tests – Determinism
dimensions.evidence: The local oracle and the local oracle re-run give identical results (reward 1.0, f2p 7/7, p2p 2/2), matching the CB Oracle. The local nop and the stubbed nop both fail the same 7 f2p with the same values (e.g. 278.8665°). Box2D steps at a fixed BOX2D_TIME_STEP, and missile.act() uses the same step, so the flame animation time is deterministic. Textures are Mockito mocks, so no fonts or image loading are involved. The GL tests run in a hidden software-GL context (Xvfb, LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1). Nothing uses the network or wall-clock time. test.sh runs `./gradlew --no-daemon --offline` and installs nothing at test time; the Dockerfile pre-warms every jar.

dimensions.name: Hardening – Real & Feasible
dimensions.evidence: Defect 1 is upstream issue #362 (PR #373): the carried rocket is drawn over foreground map elements. Bugs 01-05 are plausible developer mistakes: a degrees/radians mix-up hidden behind normalizeAnglePiRad, a joint reference angle that keeps the wrong offset, a sprite axis swap for the exhaust, a radians-for-degrees mix-up in BodyRegionDrawer, a sign flip in the car shadow offset, and a +Y look-ahead rotated by (90 - heading). Each fix is a one- or two-line correction a real developer would write. The z-order fix is the upstream restructure, and simpler valid fixes also pass. Feasible: afXQArC solved all six from the video and the code.
